Definition: from G853; disappearance, i.e. (figuratively) abrogation:--vanish away.
BiblicalUsage: Vanishing away — the old covenant is ready to vanish away, made old by the new one. The word is about something fading out because its time is done.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the old covenant vanished because the new one arrived, and Christ is the reason it could go.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
